result.stdout:
Create a new Rask project from a template.

Usage: rask new <name> [options]

Arguments:
  <name>   Name of the project to create (scaffolds ./<name>/).

Options:
  -t, --template <name>   Template to scaffold (default: server). [server|wasm|wasm-hosted|native]
  -o, --output <dir>      Directory to create the project in (default: ./<name>).
  -n, --name <name>       Project name, if not given positionally.
      --host <mode>       Native template only: where the UI comes from — 'native' runs the components on the device (default), 'server' or 'wasm-hosted' make the app a thin native shell over a Rask app you host. [native|server|wasm-hosted]
      --platform <name>   Native template only: a platform to target, repeatable (default: both). Only the chosen platforms get a TFM, a manifest and a head. [ios|android]
      --auth              Add cookie authentication (login + members pages).
      --pwa               Add a PWA manifest, icon, and offline page.
      --cqrs              Wire up Rask.Cqrs. On 'wasm-hosted' this also makes the client dispatch to the server — no HttpClient, no endpoints to write.
      --data              Pre-wire a database + EF Core: an AppDbContext your features map through (server only).
      --docker            Add a Dockerfile and .dockerignore for container deploys.
      --no-restore        Don't run dotnet restore after scaffolding (for offline use).
      --no-git            Don't initialize a git repository (one is created with an initial commit by default).
      --no-bootstrap      Render pages with plain elements and a small built-in stylesheet instead of Rask.Bootstrap.
      --force             Scaffold into a directory that already has files in it, overwriting on collision.
      --jobs              Durable background jobs on the app's own database (implies --data).
      --mail              Transactional email queued on the app's own database (implies --data).
      --cache             A database-backed ICache + IDistributedCache (implies --data).
      --outbox

result.stdout:
Run the app with hot reload (dotnet watch).

Usage: rask dev [options] [-- <args passed to the app>]

Arguments:
  [-- <args>]   Everything after '--' is passed to your app, not to rask.

Options:
  -p, --project <path>          Project to run (default: the project in the current directory).
      --urls <url[;url]>        URLs the app should listen on (sets ASPNETCORE_URLS).
      --launch-profile <name>   launchSettings profile to use.
      --open                    Open the app in your browser once it is listening.
      --no-open                 Never open a browser.
      --no-hot-reload           Restart on change instead of applying edits live (still watches).
      --no-restart              Ask before restarting on an edit hot reload can't apply.
      --once                    Run once without watching (plain 'dotnet run').
      --no-banner               Suppress the startup banner.
      --dry-run                 Print the command that would run without starting anything.

Examples:
  rask dev
  rask dev --open
  rask dev --project src/App
  rask dev --urls http://localhost:5000
  rask dev -- --my-app-flag

result.stdout:
Manage EF Core migrations, and back the database up or restore it.

Usage: rask db <action> [<name|file>] [options] [-- <ef args>]

Arguments:
  [<name|file>]   Migration name for 'add' (e.g. InitialCreate), or the backup file for 'restore'.

Actions:
  add       Create a migration from the current model.
  remove    Delete the most recent migration.
  list      List the migrations and which are applied.
  update    Apply pending migrations to the database.
  drop      Delete the database and everything in it.
  backup    Copy the database to a file.
  restore   Replace the database from a backup file.

Options:
  -p, --project <path>           Project containing the DbContext (default: found from the current directory).
  -s, --startup-project <path>   Startup project (default: same as --project).
  -c, --context <Name>           DbContext to use when the project defines more than one.
  -o, --output <path>            Migration output directory (add), or the backup file or directory to write (backup).
      --remote                   Act on the deployed database instead of the local one (backup, restore).
      --host <user@host>         Deployment host for --remote (default: the one in .rask/deploy.json).
      --app <name>               Deployed app name for --remote (default: the one in .rask/deploy.json).
  -y, --yes                      Skip the confirmation prompt (drop, restore).
      --dry-run                  Print what would run without touching the database.
      --json                     Print the result as JSON instead of a human-readable report.

Examples:
  rask db add InitialCreate
  rask db update
  rask db list
  rask db drop --yes
  rask db backup
  rask db backup --remote --output backups/
  rask db restore backups/shop-20260805-081500.db --remote

result.stdout:
Build and deploy the app to a single host over SSH (auto-HTTPS with --domain).

Usage: rask deploy [<action>] [options]

Arguments:
  [<action>]   Operate on what's already deployed instead of deploying (omit to deploy).

Actions:
  status     Show what is running, and on which color.
  logs       Print the deployed app's logs.
  rollback   Put the previous image back.

Options:
      --host <user@box>                         SSH target to build and run on (remembered in .rask/deploy.json).
  -d, --domain <host>                           Public domain to serve over HTTPS via Caddy (implies ports 80/443).
      --port <n>                                Published port when not using --domain (default: 8080).
      --container-port <n>                      Port the app listens on inside the container (default: 8080; remembered).
  -p, --project <path>                          Project to deploy (default: found from the current directory).
  -n, --name <slug>                             Container/app name (default: derived from the project).
      --dockerfile <path>                       Dockerfile to build (default: ./Dockerfile).
      --env-file <path>                         File of KEY=VALUE lines to pass to the container.
  -e, --env <KEY=VALUE>                         Environment variable to pass (repeatable).
      --health-path <path>                      HTTP path probed for readiness before the blue-green swap (default: /health).
      --no-health-check                         Skip the post-deploy HTTP health check.
      --github-actions                          Write a .github/workflows/deploy.yml that runs this deploy on push, and print the secrets to add.
      --dry-run                                 Print the docker commands that would run without changing anything.
      --json                                    Print the result as JSON instead of a human-readable report.
      --tail <n>                                Log lines to show (logs only; default: 100, 'all' for everything).
  -f, --follo
[truncated]

Print a shell completion script (bash, zsh, or fish).

Usage: rask completion <shell>

Actions:
  bash   A bash completion function.
  zsh    A zsh completion function.
  fish   Fish completion definitions.

Examples:
  rask completion bash >> ~/.bashrc
  rask completion zsh > "${fpath[1]}/_rask"
  rask completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/rask.fish
